Niemirow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Niemirów, Poland

Demolished. The Niemirów cemetery, likely established in the first half of the 19th century for a community first documented in 1807, was devastated beginning in WWII — unconfirmed reports say its matzevot were used to help build Soviet-era Molotov Line fortifications between 1939 and 1941. Afterward the site was ploughed and planted with birch trees, now a distinctive monoculture forest marking its former boundaries. This record's gravestone-count field reads '1945' — almost certainly the postwar afforestation date rather than an actual tombstone count, similar to a data mix-up flagged elsewhere in this batch, so it's noted here rather than reported as fact. Restitution proceedings over the site are reportedly still pending.
